hints: Focus on what alkaline $\text{I}_2$ really tests for, the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group or the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group.
Notice that Y must be able to form two $\text{-COO}^-$ groups, so it needs two separate sites that can both give the iodoform reaction.
Check which diol leaves only $\text{CH}_2$ groups between the two new carboxylic acid carbons after both $\text{CH}_3$ groups are lost as $\text{CHI}_3$.
walkthrough:
**Recall the iodoform reaction**

Alkaline $\text{I}_2$ first oxidises $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ to $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$, then cleaves it. Think of it simply as:
$$\text{R-CH(OH)-CH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{I}_2 / \text{OH}^-} \text{R-COO}^- + \text{CHI}_3$$
The $\text{CH}_3$ is lost as yellow $\text{CHI}_3$, and the rest of the molecule becomes a carboxylate.

**Apply this to a diol**

To finish with a dicarboxylic acid $\text{HOOC-R-COOH}$, Y must react twice, so it must contain two $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ groups. One reaction gives one $\text{-COO}^-$, two reactions give two $\text{-COO}^-$ groups.

**Test pentan-2,4-diol**

Pentan-2,4-diol is $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH(OH)-CH}_2\text{-CH(OH)-CH}_3$. It is symmetrical with a $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ unit at each end.
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{I}_2 / \text{OH}^-} {}^-\text{OOC-CH}_2\text{-COO}^- + 2\text{CHI}_3$$
After acidification:
$$ {}^-\text{OOC-CH}_2\text{-COO}^- \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+} \text{HOOC-CH}_2\text{-COOH} $$
This is propanedioic acid, which fits $\text{HOOC-R-COOH}$ with $\text{R} = \text{CH}_2$.

options.A: Pentan-1,4-diol is $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$. It has only one $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group, so only one iodoform cleavage occurs to give $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^-$. On acidification this gives a hydroxy acid, not a dicarboxylic acid.
options.B: Pentan-1,5-diol is $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. It has no $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group and no $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group, so it gives a negative iodoform test and does not react with alkaline $\text{I}_2$ in this way.
options.C: Pentan-2,3-diol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. It has only one $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ end that can be cleaved. The product is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)COO}^-$, which gives 2-hydroxybutanoic acid on acidification, a monocarboxylic hydroxy acid, not $\text{HOOC-R-COOH}$.
options.D: Pentan-2,4-diol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$ with two $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ groups. Both ends undergo iodoform cleavage, losing 2 $\text{CHI}_3$ and leaving $^-\text{OOC-CH}_2\text{-COO}^-$. Acidification gives $\text{HOOC-CH}_2\text{-COOH}$, a dicarboxylic acid where R is one $\text{CH}_2$ group.
